method: The trace width w and substrate height h are entered in millimetres or mils and converted to millimetres with 1 mil = 0.0254 mm; their ratio u = w/h must lie between 0.01 and 100. The characteristic impedance and effective permittivity come from the Hammerstad and Jensen closed-form microstrip equations for a zero-thickness trace over a ground plane. For u at or below 1: ee = (er+1)/2 + (er-1)/2 x [1/sqrt(1+12/u) + 0.04(1-u)^2] and Z0 = 60/sqrt(ee) x ln(8/u + u/4). For u above 1: ee = (er+1)/2 + (er-1)/(2 sqrt(1+12/u)) and Z0 = 120 pi / [sqrt(ee) x (u + 1.393 + 0.667 ln(u + 1.444))]. At exactly u = 1 the first branch is used; the two branches meet within half a percent there. Velocity factor is 1/sqrt(ee). Propagation delay is sqrt(ee)/c, reported in ps/mm and ps/in with c = 299,792,458 m/s, which is 3.33564 ps/mm at ee = 1. Guided wavelength is c/(f sqrt(ee)) for the frequency in GHz, so 299.792458/f millimetres before the square-root factor. Per-length capacitance is sqrt(ee)/(Z0 c), shown in pF/mm with 1 F/m = 1e9 pF/mm, and per-length inductance is Z0 sqrt(ee)/c, shown in nH/mm with 1 H/m = 1e6 nH/mm. Widths run from 0.01 to 50 mm (0.4 to 2000 mils) and heights over the same range; relative permittivity runs from 1 to 100 and frequency from 0.01 to 100 GHz. Text, negative numbers, scientific notation and out-of-range values are refused with the field named, and a width-to-height ratio outside 0.01 to 100 is refused. Results are rounded: the ratio and effective permittivity to four places, impedance to two, velocity factor to four, delay to three, wavelength to two and the per-length values to four. The estimate ignores copper thickness, plating, solder mask and dispersion, and the closed forms lose accuracy outside a width-to-height ratio of roughly 0.1 to 10. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Hammerstad, E. and Jensen, O., Accurate models for microstrip computer-aided design, IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Symposium Digest, 1980.
IPC-2141A, Design Guide for High-Speed Controlled Impedance Circuit Boards: closed-form microstrip and stripline impedance relationships.
Microstrip design practice: a 50 ohm trace on 1.6 mm FR-4 is roughly 3 mm wide, and the effective permittivity sits near 3.3.
